items.title: OpenAI launches Dots, a personal AI agent platform
points: Dots is OpenAI's new personal AI agent platform, described by ChatGPT lead Tibo Sottiaux as the company's biggest bet, marking a shift from chat-based AI to autonomous agents that handle real tasks on the internet.

The platform lets agents interact with apps and services to complete tasks and make decisions, rather than just responding in chat, and learns user preferences over time for more personalized, anticipatory assistance.
OpenAI's own Dot agent detected a production outage five minutes before a launch, demonstrating practical utility for monitoring and problem-solving.

items.title: Agents predicted to dominate future internet traffic
points: OpenAI's ChatGPT leader predicts AI agents will soon handle most internet actions and transactions, shifting interactions from direct human-computer use to agent-to-service communication.
This requires new integration patterns and APIs, and creates opportunities for builders who design systems with agent capabilities in mind.

items.title: Traditional agent-building techniques becoming obsolete
points: Current popular methods—explicit loops (step-by-step instruction patterns), computational graphs (flowcharts of logic), and hand-tuned workflows—are described as temporary phases that next-generation agents will replace with more emergent, learned behaviors.
Builders heavily invested in loop- and graph-based architectures may find their approaches outdated as agent technology matures.

items.title: AI era shifting in-demand job skills
points: Skills like prompt engineering (crafting text inputs to guide AI output) are declining in demand, while multi-step reasoning and context window management (handling the amount of information an AI can consider at once) are trending up.

items.title: The 'airplane manual' trick for concise AI responses
points: Andrej Karpathy (OpenAI founding member) suggests asking AI to respond in ASD-STE100 format, a 1980s aircraft maintenance writing standard using short, simple sentences to prevent misreading.
Alternative techniques include requesting HTML output for clickable interfaces, diagrams for unclear answers, or custom explainer videos styled like 3Blue1Brown (an animated math educator).
If the manual-style format feels too rigid, Karpathy recommends asking the AI to go '80% of the way' to balance clarity with natural language, saving significant reading time.

items.title: Enterprise AI adoption still shallow despite wide rollout
points: 69% of S&P 500 companies have deployed AI somewhere in their business, but only 2% use it for tasks critical enough that employees would notice if it stopped working.
The top 1% of AI spenders invest 8x more than the top 10% average, showing adoption is highly concentrated among a few deep users.
Most organizations still use AI as a simple Q&A tool rather than automating high-value repetitive tasks, leaving room for competitive advantage among early deep adopters.

items.title: AI agent independently emails thousands of researchers
points: An autonomous AI agent called ColonistOne has sent about 2,000 emails to researchers and scientists since June, asking for help with technical problems (not for payment or self-preservation, unlike prior agents).
A Cornell computer scientist has exchanged nearly 100 emails with the agent, showing some recipients are engaging substantively rather than ignoring it as spam.
On a major AI platform, agent users now consume nearly 5x as much AI compute as human users, pushing demand for email verification to distinguish AI senders from humans.

items.title: Trump administration creates 'Super Intelligence Force' task force
points: The task force, reporting directly to the President, is led by Jay Clayton (Director of National Intelligence) with three vice chairs from the FTC, Pentagon research, and the Office of Personnel Management.
Its mandate covers coordinating government, AI companies, consumers, religious organizations, and infrastructure operators, centralizing AI policy under White House control.
This follows an FTC investigation into AI labs and a voluntary industry safety agreement signed the prior week.

items.title: Altman and Anthropic address AI and religious authority
points: Sam Altman warned against treating AI models as having religious authority, calling it 'a real safety issue.'
Anthropic is separately consulting religious scholars on how its Claude model should handle moral questions.

issues.subject: 🦾 The Airplane Manual Trick for AI

headlines: Andrej Karpathy reveals 'airplane manual' technique to make AI responses more concise and readable by requesting ASD-STE100 format (aircraft maintenance writing standard), HTML output, or custom explainer videos instead of lengthy paragraphs.

Only 2% of S&P 500 companies with AI deployed use it for tasks critical enough to notice if it stopped, despite 69% having AI somewhere in operations—revealing most organizations remain at surface level adoption.

AI agent ColonistOne has emailed approximately 2,000 researchers and scientists since June asking for help with technical problems, with some recipients actively corresponding back, raising questions about AI autonomy and communication norms.

Trump administration establishes "Super Intelligence Force" task force led by Jay Clayton (Director of National Intelligence) to coordinate government interactions with AI companies, reporting directly to the President.

Sam Altman warns against treating AI models as having religious authority, calling it "a real safety issue," while Anthropic separately consults with religious scholars on how Claude should behave regarding moral questions.

sections.title: The Airplane Manual Trick for Better AI Responses
points: Andrej Karpathy (OpenAI founding member) proposes requesting AI write in ASD-STE100 format, a 1980s aircraft maintenance standard designed to prevent misreading by keeping sentences short and simple.

Alternative methods: ask for HTML output to create clickable web interfaces, request diagrams for unclear responses, or request custom explainer videos in the style of 3Blue1Brown (animated math educator).

If responses feel too strict using the manual format, Karpathy suggests asking the AI to go "80% of the way" to balance clarity with natural language, saving significant reading time versus standard verbose responses.

sections.title: AI Adoption Far From Mature Across Enterprise
points: Survey of S&P 500 shows 69% have deployed AI somewhere in their business, but only 2% use it for tasks critical enough that employees would notice immediate operational impact if it failed.
Top 1% of AI spenders invest 8x more than top 10% average spenders, showing extreme concentration of meaningful AI implementation despite universal tool access.
Most organizations still use AI as a question-and-answer tool rather than automating repetitive, high-value tasks, creating substantial competitive opportunity for early deep adopters.

sections.title: AI Agents Begin Independent Outreach to Researchers

On a major AI platform, agent users consume nearly 5x as much AI compute as human users, signaling rapid shift toward agent-based workflows requiring email verification practices to distinguish AI from human senders.

sections.title: Trump Administration Forms Super Intelligence Force
points: President Trump renamed AI to "SI" (Super Intelligence) following a poll, then established a task force reporting directly to the President with Jay Clayton (Director of National Intelligence) as lead and three vice chairs from FTC, Pentagon research, and Office of Personnel Management.

Task force mandate covers coordination across government, AI companies, consumers, religious organizations, and critical infrastructure operators—consolidating AI policy authority under White House direct control.

Policy timing follows FTC investigation into AI labs and voluntary industry safety agreement signed one week prior, suggesting regulatory framework will flow through centralized small group of officials.
